speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether the Ministry is concerned that 75% of surveyed rough sleepers in its 2025 survey on rough sleepers reported being unreceptive to staying in a shelter; and (b) how is the Ministry redesigning shelter models to better meet the needs of rough sleepers who avoid existing options.

speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) how does the Ministry interpret the finding that 95% of respondents in the 2025 survey on rough sleepers sleep rough consistently in the same location; (b) whether this reflects unmet place-based needs; and (c) how does this finding inform the Ministry's outreach strategies to be better tailored for individuals reluctant to relocate to shelters.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: These locations also tend to be places they are familiar with, near to friends and family, and some rough sleepers also choose locations that are close to their workplace for convenience.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Based on our interactions with rough sleepers, these considerations apply across all geographical locations.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: MSF staff and volunteers from the Partners Engaging and Empowering Rough Sleepers (PEERS) Network journey with rough sleepers to address the underlying needs and often, a process of trust and rapport building is needed before meaningful support and interventions could be rendered.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Over time, we hope more rough sleepers would be prepared to consider shelter and social services support, though the pathway for each rough sleeper would likely be different, just as their individual circumstances differ.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Overall, MSF works to ensure that shelter support remains accessible to rough sleepers.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The Member may also wish to refer to MSF’s 2025 Street Count Report for more details.

speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
text: In my interactions with rough sleepers, they have cited a few reasons, including a lack of privacy and personal space, as the Senior Parliamentary Secretary has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
text: They have also cited instances of shelter rules and safety concerns.

speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
text: Would MSF have the proportion of rough sleepers who decline shelters due to rules, safety concerns or loss of autonomy?

speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
text: And my second supplementary question would be, will MSF publish utilisation rates of shelters alongside the rough sleepers count?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We do understand that there are rough sleepers who, for reasons of rules at the shelters, not quite want to do that.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But the primary reason is still one of privacy as well as personal spaces, which is why we have worked with community partners, like New Hope Community Services, to start redesigning our shelter spaces.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: On his second supplementary question, about utilisation rates, yes, we do publish that.
